neighbours.label: first-person informal statement of personal need or wish ('I really need to', 'I needed', 'I wish')
fire: Ugh, this week has been endless. I really need a nap before dinner.
Loved the class so much, honestly I need to sign up for the next one.
Thanks for the kind words, I needed that today more than you know.
The pool was gorgeous and I wish we could have stayed another night.
My closet is a disaster. I seriously need to get rid of half these clothes.
That pasta was amazing, I need the recipe as soon as possible!
Back from vacation and I already need another one, lol.
Such a fun weekend with the girls, I needed a break like that.
quiet: The bridge needs structural repairs before it can reopen to traffic.
Applicants need a valid passport and two letters of reference.
The software requires at least four gigabytes of memory to run.
Most houseplants need indirect light and water once a week.
The report needs to be submitted to the board by the end of June.
Seedlings need warmth and moisture during their first two weeks.
The museum will need new funding to keep the east wing open.
Patients with diabetes need regular checks of their blood sugar.

predictions: Casual first-person 'I need/needed/wish' sentences fire around the verb; impersonal or third-person 'need' in formal prose stays quiet.
notes: Probe: 'I really need to though' 0.452, 'I need to go home and think' 0.481, 'I needed the reminder' 0.257, 'I wish I had' 0.323 (peak ' I'), 'I really want to visit' 0.233; 'The engine needs a new gasket' 0.014, 'The committee will need additional data' 0.012. Card examples are blog and hotel-review voice.
